sources.entry: beanie - An asynchronous Python object-document mapper (ODM) for MongoDB.

summary.one_liner: Beanie is an asynchronous Python object-document mapper (ODM) for MongoDB, with data models built on Pydantic.
summary.what_it_does: Each MongoDB collection maps to a Beanie Document class that is used to query, insert, update, and delete documents in that collection. Models are Pydantic models, so normal Python types and nested Pydantic models can be used as fields. Fields can be marked as indexed, and queries can be written with Python comparison syntax (for example, Product.price < 10). Documents can be updated with methods such as set(). The README states that data and schema migrations are supported out of the box. It is built on the PyMongo async client. A synchronous counterpart, Bunnet, is mentioned. The README also links to example projects using FastAPI and to articles on projections, relations, cache, and actions.
use_cases: Async MongoDB access from Python web apps
Defining typed document schemas with Pydantic
Querying MongoDB with Python expressions instead of raw queries
Adding indexes to MongoDB collection fields
Running data or schema migrations on MongoDB collections
Building FastAPI backends backed by MongoDB
how_to_run: Initialize with init_beanie(database=client.db_name, document_models=[...]) using a PyMongo AsyncMongoClient
Define Document subclasses and call insert(), find_one(), and set() on them
notable: Documents behave like Pydantic models and are saved to the matching MongoDB collection
Built-in data and schema migration support
Pythonic query syntax using model field attributes
caveats: The README says v3 is under active development and that reviews and responses on issues and PRs may be slower than usual
Requires a MongoDB server; the README does not describe other databases
